name: Cagrilintide

what.text: Cagrilintide is an experimental injected peptide from Novo Nordisk. It is a long-acting version of amylin, a hormone the pancreas releases that makes people feel full. It is given once a week under the skin in trials.

src.label: Lau et al., cagrilintide phase 2, Lancet

what.text: Most trials test it combined with semaglutide 2.4 mg, the dose in Wegovy. That combination is called CagriSema. Novo Nordisk is also testing cagrilintide by itself in Phase 3.

src.label: Garvey et al., REDEFINE 1, N Engl J Med
RENEW 1 trial record, ClinicalTrials.gov

what.text: It is not approved anywhere the search checked. FDA says it is not a part of any FDA-approved drug and has not been found safe and effective for any condition.

research.text: Cagrilintide has been tested in randomized trials paid for by Novo Nordisk, alone and with semaglutide. The main ones are listed below as they were run. The Phase 3 program for the combination is called REDEFINE.

research.title: Phase 2: cagrilintide alone for weight

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, with an open active comparator (liraglutide 3.0 mg)
706 adults without diabetes, with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with high blood pressure or high blood fats
weekly cagrilintide 0.3, 0.6, 1.2, 2.4 or 4.5 mg; daily liraglutide 3.0 mg; or placebo

research.found: Weight fell by 6.0% to 10.8% on cagrilintide, 9.0% on liraglutide and 3.0% on placebo. Stomach and bowel side effects, mainly nausea, happened in 41% to 63% on cagrilintide and 32% on placebo. 10% stopped treatment early, at similar rates across groups. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03856047.

src.label: Lau et al., cagrilintide phase 2, Lancet

research.title: REDEFINE 1: CagriSema in adults without diabetes

facts.v: Phase 3a, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled
3,417 adults without diabetes, with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with an obesity-related condition
weekly cagrilintide 2.4 mg plus semaglutide 2.4 mg (2,108 people), semaglutide alone (302), cagrilintide alone (302) or placebo (705), all with lifestyle support
percent change in body weight; share losing at least 5%

research.found: Average weight changed by -20.4% on the combination and -3.0% on placebo. Stomach and bowel side effects (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, belly pain) affected 79.6% on the combination and 39.9% on placebo, mostly short-lived and mild to moderate. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05567796.

src.label: Garvey et al., REDEFINE 1, N Engl J Med
REDEFINE 1 trial record, ClinicalTrials.gov

research.title: REDEFINE 2: CagriSema in adults with type 2 diabetes

facts.v: 1,206 adults with type 2 diabetes, a BMI of 27 or more and HbA1c of 7% to 10%
weekly cagrilintide 2.4 mg plus semaglutide 2.4 mg, or placebo, with lifestyle support
percent change in body weight; share losing at least 5%

research.found: Average weight changed by -13.7% on the combination and -3.4% on placebo. 73.5% and 15.9% reached an HbA1c of 6.5% or less. Stomach and bowel side effects affected 72.5% and 34.4%. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05394519.

src.label: Davies et al., REDEFINE 2, N Engl J Med
REDEFINE 2 trial record, ClinicalTrials.gov

research.text: Still running: REDEFINE 3, a heart-outcome trial of CagriSema in about 7,100 people due to finish in 2027, and RENEW 1, a Phase 3 trial of cagrilintide alone in about 300 people.

after.text: Cagrilintide is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. The 2026 List's class S0 (non-approved substances) bans, at all times, any drug that is not covered by another section of the List and has no current approval from any government health regulator for human use. It names drugs still in clinical development as an example. The 2027 List keeps this class and adds peptides to its examples. The search found no approval for cagrilintide anywhere, so that class’s wording may cover it. WADA has not ruled on it. Semaglutide, its partner in CagriSema, is approved and is on WADA’s 2027 Monitoring Program, which tracks use without banning it.
